issues.legal_issue: The exclusion of other parcels from an acquisition does not entitle an owner to exclusion where the other parcels were excluded for different or unknown reasons and the owner’s land is integral to the scheme.
material_facts: Some comparison parcels had been excluded, but one was involved in pending litigation and another was far inside the area, with no material explaining its exclusion.
Other parcels had been excluded by a Reference Court, and appeals concerning those exclusions were pending.
Government guidelines for excluding certain lands had been withdrawn after the Government recognized their harmful effect on housing schemes.
The respondents’ land abutted a main road and was practically the gateway to the scheme; excluding it would frustrate the scheme.
issues.conclusion: The respondents were not entitled to exclusion of their land, and the different exclusions did not establish invidious discrimination or arbitrary exercise of power.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 does not require identical treatment where the circumstances or reasons for other exclusions are different, unknown, or not established. The withdrawn guidelines could not support a claim to exclusion, particularly where exclusion of the land would frustrate the scheme.

rule.if: land_acquisition_challenge and other_parcels_excluded and comparator_exclusions_have_distinct_or_unknown_basis and challenged_land_is_essential_to_scheme and exclusion_guidelines_withdrawn

predicates.land_acquisition_challenge: An owner challenges the acquisition of land for a public scheme.
predicates.other_parcels_excluded: The government or a court has excluded other parcels from the scheme.
predicates.comparator_exclusions_have_distinct_or_u: The reasons for excluding the other parcels are different from, or not established to be the same as, the reasons relevant to the challenged land.
predicates.challenged_land_is_essential_to_scheme: The challenged land occupies a position such that excluding it would frustrate the scheme.
predicates.exclusion_guidelines_withdrawn: The government withdrew the guidelines that had been relied on to support exclusion of land.
predicates.equal_treatment_does_not_require_exclusi: The owner is not entitled to exclusion merely because other parcels were excluded.

issues.definition: When an owner challenges an acquisition, other parcels were excluded for distinct or unknown reasons, the challenged land is essential to the scheme, and the relevant exclusion guidelines were withdrawn, equal treatment does not require exclusion.

issues.legal_issue: An erratum correcting the omission of land from an acquisition notification does not invalidate the declaration where the affected owners had the opportunity to participate in, and did participate in, the objection inquiry.
material_facts: An erratum added lands in survey numbers that had been omitted because they lay in adjacent villages.
The respondents had the opportunity to object and in fact participated in the inquiry into objections.
The respondents argued that no separate inquiry was held after publication of the erratum.
issues.conclusion: The erratum related back to the original notification and was not a fresh notification; the declaration was not invalidated by the absence of a separate inquiry after the erratum.
issues.legal_principle: An erratum correcting an omission in the original notification dates back to that notification and is not a fresh notification. Where affected owners had the opportunity to participate and did participate in the inquiry under Section 5A and Rule 3, the declaration under Section 6 is not vitiated merely because there was no separate inquiry after the erratum.

rule.if: land_acquisition_challenge and erratum_corrected_omitted_land and owners_participated_in_objection_inquiry and no_separate_post_erratum_inquiry

predicates.land_acquisition_challenge: An owner challenges a declaration made in a land acquisition proceeding.
predicates.erratum_corrected_omitted_land: An erratum corrected an omission of the owner’s land from the original notification.
predicates.owners_participated_in_objection_inquiry: The affected owners had the opportunity to object and participated in the inquiry into their objections.
predicates.no_separate_post_erratum_inquiry: No separate objection inquiry was conducted after publication of the erratum.
predicates.declaration_not_invalidated_by_lack_of_n: The declaration remains valid despite the absence of a separate inquiry after the erratum.

issues.definition: When an erratum corrects an omission, the owners participated in the objection inquiry, and no separate inquiry followed the erratum, the declaration is not invalidated for that reason.

issues.legal_issue: A prior ruling that an acquisition scheme was vague cannot support quashing the acquisition when the controversy has since been considered by a larger bench of the Supreme Court.
material_facts: The High Court’s Division Bench quashed the acquisition on the ground that the scheme was vague, following an earlier Supreme Court decision.
A three-judge bench of the Supreme Court had subsequently considered the controversy concerning vagueness and failure to make the scheme.
issues.conclusion: The Division Bench’s decision quashing the acquisition on that basis could not be sustained.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on State of Tamil Nadu v. L. Krishnan, decided by a three-judge bench, which had considered the controversy concerning vagueness and failure to make the scheme; the earlier reliance on State of Tamil Nadu v. A. Mohammed Yusuf did not sustain the High Court’s ruling after that consideration.

predicates.land_acquisition_challenge: An owner challenges an acquisition proceeding.
predicates.acquisition_quashed_for_scheme_vagueness: A court quashed the acquisition on the ground that the scheme was vague or had not been made.
predicates.larger_bench_has_considered_that_controv: A larger bench of the Supreme Court has already considered the controversy concerning the scheme’s vagueness or failure to make the scheme.
predicates.acquisition_not_quashed_on_that_vaguenes: The acquisition cannot be quashed on that vagueness ground.

issues.definition: When an acquisition challenge relies on a ruling that the scheme was vague and a larger bench has considered that controversy, the acquisition is not quashed on that ground.

issues.legal_issue: A later award for a parcel does not invalidate an earlier award made within the applicable period, and a stay of dispossession prevents the acquisition proceedings from being treated as barred by the limitation period.
material_facts: An initial award was made within two years of the relevant declaration.
A later award was made for one survey parcel.
There was a stay of dispossession, which prevented further proceedings from going forward.
issues.conclusion: The later award did not invalidate the initial award, and the stay of dispossession meant that the limitation period did not bar the proceedings.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 11 and 11A of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, an initial award made within the prescribed period is not invalidated merely because a later award is made for a particular parcel. Under the proviso to Section 11A, a stay of dispossession prevents the limitation period from operating as a bar to further proceedings.

rule.if: land_acquisition_proceeding and initial_award_within_applicable_period and later_award_for_particular_parcel and dispossession_stayed

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: An authority is carrying out a land acquisition proceeding.
predicates.initial_award_within_applicable_period: The authority made an initial award within the applicable period.
predicates.later_award_for_particular_parcel: The authority later made a separate award for a particular parcel.
predicates.dispossession_stayed: A court stayed dispossession, preventing further proceedings from going forward.
predicates.later_award_and_stay_do_not_invalidate_a: The later award does not invalidate the initial award, and the stay prevents the limitation period from barring further proceedings.

issues.definition: When an initial award is timely, a later award covers a particular parcel, and dispossession is stayed, the later award and stay do not invalidate the acquisition.

issues.legal_issue: An irregularity in serving notices concerning compensation and persons interested in acquired land is curable and does not by itself invalidate the award.
material_facts: The respondents alleged that notices had been served on many persons on a single day, including a deceased person.
The Court held that even an irregularity in service of the notices would be curable and would not invalidate the award.
issues.conclusion: Any irregularity in service of the notices did not make the award invalid.
issues.legal_principle: An irregularity in service of notices under Sections 9 and 10 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, is curable and does not invalidate an award made under Section 11.

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: An authority is making an award in a land acquisition proceeding.
predicates.compensation_notices_served_irregularly: The authority served notices concerning compensation or interested persons in an irregular manner.
predicates.service_irregularity_is_curable: The defect in service is an irregularity that can be cured.
predicates.award_not_invalidated_by_service_irregul: The award remains valid despite the curable service irregularity.

issues.definition: When notices in a land acquisition proceeding were served irregularly but the defect is curable, the award is not invalidated by that defect.

issues.legal_issue: Taking possession by a memorandum or panchanama vests acquired land in the State, and an erstwhile owner’s later continued occupation does not undo that vesting.
material_facts: The State took possession by a memorandum or panchanama and handed the land to the Housing Board.
The respondents contended that they had physically remained in possession.
The Court held that physical possession could not be taken in the manner asserted and that any continued occupation was unlawful.
issues.conclusion: The land vested absolutely in the State upon possession being taken, and any subsequent continued occupation by the former owners neither bound the State nor divested the State of title.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 16 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, land vests in the State free from encumbrances when possession is taken. Taking possession by a memorandum or panchanama is a legally accepted method; subsequent occupation by the former owner does not divest the State of the vested title.

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: An authority has acquired land in a land acquisition proceeding.
predicates.possession_recorded_by_memorandum_or_pan: The authority recorded the taking of possession by a memorandum or panchanama.
predicates.former_owner_continued_occupying_afterwa: The former owner continued to occupy the land after possession was recorded as taken.
predicates.vesting_is_not_undone_by_later_occupatio: The State’s vesting of title is not undone by the former owner’s later occupation.

issues.definition: When possession is recorded by a memorandum or panchanama and the former owner continues to occupy the land afterward, that later occupation does not undo vesting.

issues.legal_issue: Delay in making an award does not justify setting aside the acquisition where the statutory additional amount and interest adequately compensate for the resulting loss.
material_facts: The respondents had been denied enjoyment of the land between the taking of possession and the deposit of compensation.
The award was delayed.
The Court held that the additional amount and interest provided under the amended compensation provisions adequately compensated the respondents for any loss.
issues.conclusion: The respondents were adequately compensated for the delay and were not entitled to have the award set aside or to further compensation on that basis.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 23(1A) and 28 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, as amended by Act 68 of 1984, provide an additional amount and interest to compensate for delay in making an award and for loss of enjoyment between taking possession and deposit. The Court considered that compensation adequate in this case.

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: An owner challenges an award made in a land acquisition proceeding.
predicates.award_delayed: The authority delayed making the award.
predicates.statutory_additional_compensation_and_in: The additional compensation and interest available in the proceeding adequately compensate for the loss caused by the delay.
predicates.delay_does_not_justify_setting_aside_awa: The delay does not justify setting aside the award or granting further compensation on that basis.

issues.definition: When an award is delayed but the available additional compensation and interest adequately cover the resulting loss, the delay does not justify setting aside the award or granting extra compensation.
